questions.q: What is the key difference between Post message in a chat or channel and Post an adaptive card ... and wait for a response?
options: There is no real difference; they're aliases for the same action
The adaptive card action posts a structured JSON card and pauses the flow until someone responds, while Post message just sends one-way text
Post message only works in private chats, never in channels
Adaptive cards can only be posted by a tenant administrator
questions.explain: Post message in a chat or channel is a one-way plain text/HTML notification. The adaptive card action posts an interactive JSON card and actually pauses flow execution until a response comes back.

questions.q: What is the single most common reason a brand-new flow's Teams action silently fails on its first run?
options: The flow was never saved
The Workflows app isn't installed in the target Microsoft Teams
Teams doesn't support any Power Automate actions
The channel name contains a space
questions.explain: Teams connector actions require the Workflows app to be installed in Teams (from the app store or by a tenant admin) before they can post anything.

questions.q: What format is an adaptive card's content written in before it's pasted into the Message field?
options: Plain HTML
A Markdown document
JSON, following the adaptive card schema with a body and an actions array
A PowerPoint slide exported as XML
questions.explain: Adaptive cards are defined as JSON with a type, a body array of content blocks, and an actions array of buttons like Submit.

questions.q: Which part of an adaptive card's JSON is specifically what turns it into something a person can click and respond to, rather than just read?
options: The $schema field at the top
A TextBlock element
An Input.ChoiceSet block (paired with an Action.Submit button)
The card's version number
questions.explain: TextBlock elements are just display text. An Input.ChoiceSet block provides selectable options, and combined with an Action.Submit button, it makes the card interactive.

questions.q: In the Castlebridge Logistics dock-door poll example, why does the flow use the adaptive card action instead of Post message in a chat or channel?
options: Post message is deprecated and no longer works
The flow needs to collect a dispatcher's choice of dock door and then act on that specific response, which requires waiting for an interactive reply
Adaptive cards are required for any message sent to a channel
Plain text messages cannot be sent to channels, only to individuals
questions.explain: Because the flow needs an actual selected answer to act on (which door was picked), it needs the adaptive card's wait-for-response behavior, not a one-way notification.
